notes:
Maintainer risk: MEDIUM — The three unimplemented stub functions (verify_scts, build_path, validate_attribute_cert) all return misleading operational errors instead of a not-implemented signal; these will cause integration bugs. The OcspChecker's serial-only CertID matching is a documented but real security gap that will be missed by callers who don't read the full Limitations section. The TBS 8 KiB fixed buffer produces confusing error messages for valid certs. The chain-simple crate's allowlist rejects all public-PKI TLS certs despite claiming to handle them.
Confidence: 15% chance of missed bug. Least confident flags: the pathLenConstraint calculation (i-1 formula) is correct but subtle — I verified it manually against RFC 5280 but did not run PKITS §4.5 path-length tests. Uncertainty driven by: not tracing through the full PKITS test suite to confirm all boundary conditions; not reviewing the PKITS test infrastructure in tests/pkits_4_1_4_2.rs / pkits_4_3.rs. Would raise confidence if: ran the PKITS tests and confirmed all 4.5.x (pathLenConstraint) cases pass.
Idiom rating: ACCEPTABLE — No unsafe code (all crates have #![forbid(unsafe_code)]). No .unwrap() in production paths. Error types are #[non_exhaustive] enums throughout. The main idiom issues are: (1) FetchError::Transport(String) loses error chain; (2) CertPool missing IntoIterator; (3) for-loop extension searches that should be .find().and_then() chains; (4) duplicated OID literals. None are soundness issues.
Rust idiom confidence: 10% chance of missed issue. Least confident flags: did not exhaustively check lifetime elision across all trait signatures (there are very few explicit lifetime annotations in the codebase — mostly clean). Uncertainty driven by: pkix-revocation-http and pkix-path-builder are unimplemented stubs; their idiom issues are low-signal.
title: Review: full project fresh-eyes pass
